newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - All Blacks wary of Fiji, says Marshall.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - All Blacks wary of Fiji, says Marshall.

text.p: AUCKLAND, June 13 - Halfback Justin Marshall says the All Blacks have a very real reason to be wary when they play Fiji in the one-off rugby test at Albany on Saturday.
While Fiji are generally being regarded as a regulation easy-beat warm up for the All Blacks, Marshall says that is not the case.
The fact that the All Blacks, under the guise of the New Zealand Barbarians, didn't play well in last weekend's trial and Fiji's recent record is needling the Cantabrian.
Fiji lost to South Africa 43-18 last year after trailing 16-8 with only 20 minutes to play.
They then returned home and thrashed Manu Samoa 60-0, a result that suggested a renaissance in their game.
On the current tour of New Zealand they fared far better than the touring Ireland A team, including a very good win over the newly formed Central Vikings who boasted nine Super 12 players.
It is reason enough for the All Blacks to be wary, Marshall said.
"Their backs are playing like backs and they're playing very structured rugby which is the thing to do -- and not try and play sevens rugby in the 15-man game," Marshall observed.
"They're a very dangerous side and they showed that last year in South Africa, we're well aware of that.
"We can't afford to look past this game on Saturday, we're really focused on this one."
Marshall said he and first five-eighth Andrew Mehrtens were aware Fiji would try to target the pair in an effort to cut down ball to the outside backs.
The Fijians on tour have defended well close in and around the fringes of the rucks and mauls.
"They're aggressive tacklers and that is always going to be part and parcel of their game," Marshall said.
"Most teams like to target the inside backs and get into them, but that is something Andrew and I need to get on top of.
"We've played together a lot and we know what to do in those circumstances. I'd be very pleased if they came through on the inside looking to put pressure on us.
"If they did that then we've got some talent out wide and we can spread it wide and let them do the damage out there."
He said the All Blacks were keen to do well following their poor showing in the trial.
"This test match is reality for us, we need to go up 50 percent on where we were last weekend."
And he cast a cautious eye toward his opponent Jacob Rauluni of Queensland who has steadily regained form through the tour.
The pair played each other for their respective provinces and Marshall says his memory will serve him well.
"He is a good player, very dangerous. He is bit of a confidence player but he needs to be watched as do the others," the All Black halfback said.
"He likes running with the ball as I have noticed in the games through the tour. He has a strong physical presence about him and I think he's got a very solid allround game."
Marshall says his personal goal is to improve his game after four weeks out because of a sternum injury.
More importantly than that, he wants to continue to establish his credentials as being among the best in the world.
"My game has progressed over the last couple of years, that is the calibre of players I've been involved with and I've been very lucky in that," he said.
Team:

All Blacks: Christian Cullen, Jeff Wilson, Frank Bunce, Tana Umaga, Lee Stensness, Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall, Taine Randell, Josh Kronfeld, Ian Jones, Robin Brooke, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick (capt) Craig Dowd. Reserves: Ofisa Tonu'u, Scott McLeod, Glen Osborne, Carlos Spencer, Mark Allen, Anton Oliver, Charles Riechelmann, Mark Carter.
